title: Fixed-bimodule derived adjunction normalized by evaluation and scalar restriction
statement:
Let $S\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $U:D(B)\to D(S)$ be restriction of scalars in the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix a K-flat $B$-complex $Q$ [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For $Y\in D(S)$ with K-injective representative $I$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], let $J_Q(Y)$ be represented by $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(UQ,I)$ with action $(bh)(e)=h(be)$; use the canonical resolved-model comparisons of [lem-trf-bimodule-resolved-hom-tensor-models]. Let $F_Q([C])=[U\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_B Q)]$ for a $B$-complex $C$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For the chain isomorphism $\theta$ of [lem-trf-bimodule-chain-currying-descent], taking $H^0$ and the localization maps into K-injectives gives a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}([C],J_Q([I]))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S)}(F_Q([C]),[I]),\qquad [f]\longmapsto[\,c\otimes e\mapsto f(c)(e)\,].$$
Here $f:C\to\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(UQ,I)$ is a chain representative, and the inverse on a chain map $g:U\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_B Q)\to I$ is $c\mapsto(e\mapsto g(c\otimes e))$. These are the maps induced by $H^0(\theta)$ under the canonical Hom-complex identifications [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], not just an unspecified adjunction. They make $F_Q$ left adjoint to $J_Q$. Its counit is represented by the chain evaluation $U\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(UQ,I)\otimes_B Q)\to I$, $h\otimes e\mapsto h(e)$. If $r:U\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_B Q)\to N$ is a K-injective resolution over $S$, its unit at $[C]$ is represented by $c\mapsto(e\mapsto r(c\otimes e))$. The two triangle identities hold for these specified maps. For every homomorphism of commutative rings $K\to S$, restriction of every $S$-complex and $S$-map in $\theta$, the Hom-class comparison, unit, and evaluation preserves their quasi-isomorphism comparisons and commutative squares. More explicitly $\theta(sf)(c\otimes e)=s\theta(f)(c\otimes e)$, restriction retains the balancing and differential formulas, and the localized unit/counit identities retain these same representatives in $D(K)$. This means restriction of the $S$-linear Hom complexes and identities; it does not replace them by $K$-linear Hom complexes, or claim that the restricted Hom-set map is a bijection onto all $K$-linear derived morphisms. No flatness of $B/S$, perfectness of $Q$, or boundedness of $I$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09LT (lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint), specializing the differential graded algebras to commutative rings in degree zero and fixing a K-flat bimodule model; evaluation normalization from lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction.

proof.text: Put $J=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(UQ,I)$. Apply [lem-trf-bimodule-resolved-hom-tensor-models] with $T=Q$ and resolution $q=1_Q$: $J$ is K-injective over $B$, its $B$-action is the stated one, and $[\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_B Q)]$ is the canonical derived tensor model for every $C$. The same node supplies the comparison maps and the functor $J_Q$ on $D(S)$. By [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], tensoring a quasi-isomorphism in $C$ with $Q$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Forgetting to $S$ preserves it because the kernels and images have the same underlying abelian groups. Thus this tensor construction descends to $F_Q$ and uses precisely the resolved-model comparisons in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective), ordinary mixed-ring specialization supplied by the cited model node; tensor comparison as in dga.tex Tag 09LT

proof.text: For any complexes $V,W$ over a commutative ring $R$, the total Hom differential of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex] gives $Z^0\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(V,W)=\{f:d_Wf=fd_V\}$. Its degree-zero boundaries are exactly $d_Wh+hd_V$ for degree-minus-one families $h$. Hence $H^0\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(V,W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(R)}(V,W)$, sending a cocycle to its chain-homotopy class. Precomposition and postcomposition give the same operations on both sides, so these identifications are natural.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] over $B$ to target $J$ (K-injective by step 1) and over $S$ to target $I$ (K-injective by hypothesis). Combining those two localization bijections with step 2 identifies the two derived Hom sets in the statement with the two zeroth cohomology groups of $\theta$ in [lem-trf-bimodule-chain-currying-descent]. Its $H^0$ is a bijection: the isomorphism and its inverse preserve cycles and boundaries. The formulas in that node send $[f]$ to $[c\otimes e\mapsto f(c)(e)]$ and $[g]$ to $[c\mapsto(e\mapsto g(c\otimes e))]$. In particular they are the specified Hom-complex comparison, including on homotopy classes. The cited chain-currying node explicitly gives naturality under localized morphisms and canonical resolved-representative changes. Together with step 1 this proves naturality in both derived variables, not merely for chain maps.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to the inverse of the bijection of step 3. It yields $F_Q\dashv J_Q$, with unit the transpose of $1_{F_Q([C])}$ and counit the inverse transpose of $1_{J_Q([I])}$. The latter identity is represented by $1_J$; its image by the displayed formula is exactly $h\otimes e\mapsto h(e)$. For a chosen K-injective resolution $r:U\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_B Q)\to N$, the identity of $F_Q([C])$, after its canonical comparison to $[N]$, is represented by $r$. Its transpose is therefore $c\mapsto(e\mapsto r(c\otimes e))$. These are precisely the counit and unit, and the cited adjunction node gives both triangle identities for these same maps.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), adjunction-map paragraph following the definition

proof.text: Let $K\to S$ be any ring homomorphism. Restriction keeps the abelian groups and all differential maps unchanged, so it keeps kernels, images, cohomology groups, chain homotopies and quasi-isomorphisms unchanged. It therefore induces a functor $D(S)\to D(K)$ by the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The whole-complex map $\theta$ is $S$-linear by [lem-trf-bimodule-chain-currying-descent]; explicitly $\theta(sf)(c\otimes e)=(sf(c))(e)=s f(c)(e)=s\theta(f)(c\otimes e)$. Restrict each already formed $S$-complex and each $S$-linear arrow, including the comparison arrows. Their balancing and differential equations remain equalities of the same maps. Thus their commutative squares and the $H^0$/localization comparisons still commute after restriction. Evaluation remains $h\otimes e\mapsto h(e)$ and the unit remains $c\mapsto(e\mapsto r(c\otimes e))$; the localization functor preserves their identities and composites, so both triangle equalities remain true. This argument retains the $S$-linear Hom complexes: neither $I$ nor a restricted resolution is required to be K-injective over $K$, and no assertion about all $K$-linear derived morphisms is used.
